title: Compact Hosted Interaction Surface — PRD and Trimmed Launch Checklist
creator: Nina Patel
description: This document defines a compact, opinionated hosted interaction surface that covers the minimal set of endpoints for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank required for early production customers and PLG sign-ups. The goal is to reduce cognitive load for integrators, accelerate adoption, and limit operational complexity during the initial regional rollouts. The PRD focuses on constrained behaviors, default safety/quotas, and a trimmed launch checklist to enable a fast, low-friction go-live with guardrails for quality and cost.
problem_statement: Customers commonly struggle to pick an endpoint and configuration for production due to surface parity across many specialized endpoint types. That leads to integration friction, high support volume, and inconsistent metrics across customers. We need a smaller, well-documented surface that maps common patterns to sensible defaults while retaining escape hatches for advanced users.
goals: Ship a minimal, consistent hosted surface for chat, text completion, embeddings, and rerank that covers 80% of PLG use cases
Provide unambiguous default behaviors and limits to reduce support requests and misconfigurations
Ensure observability and rollback controls for the first two weeks of live traffic
Keep latency and cost within target bands for freemium and early paid tiers
non_goals: Do not introduce a full multi-protocol compatibility layer in this phase
No per-customer model customization — advanced routing remains a later Dedicated feature
No major console redesign; expose configuration via existing endpoint create flow
stakeholders: Eng: Marco Alvarez, Priya Desai (runtime), Kenji Ito (infra)
Legal & Security: SSO and KMS review owners
Customer Success: Priors for early adopters
requirements: Chat endpoint: conversational input schema, streaming support with chunked tokens, default system message that can be overridden
Completions endpoint: single-turn text generation with deterministic token limits and stop-sequence support
Embeddings endpoint: batched embedding payloads (up to 32 items), deterministic output size per model, normalized output contract
Rerank endpoint: accept list of candidates + query, return score and optional explanation field (token-limited)
Default quotas: free-tier token cap 50k/day, rate limit 30 rps for small accounts; configurable by account
Observability: per-endpoint latency P50/P95/P99 telemetry, per-model token cost breakdown, sample payload logging (redacted) for failures
Rollout controls: canary slice by account ID prefix, built-in model fallback policy for overloaded variants
Operational runbooks: clear rollback steps, degradation mode (return cached responses or simplified summary)
scope_changes_and_rationale: Removed multi-protocol parity: initial plan included full parity with legacy endpoint shapes; scoped down to canonical shapes to reduce engineering surface and accelerate launch
Deferred advanced rerank explanations: explainability field reduced to short-text reasoning to avoid leaking model internals and to lower storage for logs
Collapsed channel-specific quota settings into a single account-level quota to simplify billing and avoid early complexity for the console team
acceptance_criteria: API contract published in docs and reviewed by DX (docs acceptance)
Automated conformance tests cover chat/completions/embeddings/rerank contract with synthetic traffic and pass on staging
Performance targets met in staging: median gen latency <= 180ms for small chat requests, P95 <= 800ms for typical sequences
Cost model smoke test: per-token cost estimation within +/- 15% of runtime telemetry under representative load
Security review signed off (SSO/KMS/PII handling) and sample redaction verified
Launch checklist items completed and verified by PM, Eng lead, and Support (see launch_checklist field)
launch_checklist: Docs: quickstart, endpoint reference, migration notes, example SDK snippets (JS/Python) uploaded to docs site
Staging validation: conformance suite run twice with independent runs and flaky tests below 1%
SLOs: alerts configured for errors > 0.5% and latency regressions over 20% baseline
Quota & Billing: free-tier caps applied and billing tests for metering and invoice generation validated
Observability: dashboards created (latency, tokens, errors, top accounts) and shared with on-call
Rollout plan: define canary slice (5% seed accounts), monitor 48 hours, expand to 25% then 100% with kill-switch ready
Support readiness: CS playbook drafted, troubleshooting doc and common FAQ for misconfigurations
Security & Compliance: redaction policy live, audit logs enabled, legal sign-off acquired
E2E Smoke: sample app (in repo) demonstrates full flow for chat->embeddings->rerank with test fixture account
Post-launch eval: commit to 7-day intensive monitoring and follow-up retro with metrics and customer feedback
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha (team accounts) for 3 days -> Phase 2: 5% customer canary for 48 hours with daily checkpoints -> Phase 3: 25% expansion for 72 hours with health gating -> Phase 4: Global rollout. Each expansion requires sign-off from Eng lead and PM; rollback criteria include error rate > 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes or latency P95 doubling baseline.
telemetry_and_alerting: Token consumption per account per hour
Error rate and 5xx breakdown by model variant
Canary health dashboard with top failing accounts and recent payload samples (redacted)
Automated alert: PagerDuty if error rate > 0.5% for 15 minutes
dependencies_list: ENG-48233: Runtime kernel selection improvements (must land to meet latency targets)
ENG-49876: Metrics ingestion pipeline delta schema for token attribution
DOCS-1121: Quickstart and SDK snippet reviews
SEC-300: Security review and redaction policy implementation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected P95 latency spikes under real traffic. Mitigation: keep warm pool and implement short-circuit fallback to smaller model variant
Risk: Misconfigured stop sequences causing runaway token generation. Mitigation: hard token caps per request + server-side stop enforcement
Risk: Billing meter mismatch on day-1. Mitigation: run parallel metering and reconcile with sample accounts before billing window
Risk: Early customers hit quota constraints and experience poor UX. Mitigation: proactive communication to canary cohort and fast-track quota increases
